newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bond prices continue to rise.
newsitem.headline: Israel bond prices continue to rise.

text.p: Israeli bonds continued to rise on Sunday with prices gaining across the board amid strong demand for CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Consumer price index (CPI) linked government bonds: +0.2 pct to 168.54
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.1 pct to 165.25
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 to 157.48
"The trend of rises in CPI-linked bonds continued today as well, with surplus demand of about 142 million shekels," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities.

"The demand reflects an expectation that in the medium term inflation will go up because of higher government defence spending (because of the recent clashes between Israel and the Palestinians). Also, if the dollar starts to strengthen (against the shekel), inflation will go up," he said.
The Treasury has said that the gunbattles, which killed 73 people, would not result in higher government spending.
Halpern said expectations in the market were for the dollar to strengthen in the medium term and that demand for dollar-linked bonds would go up.
Since the political unrest began nearly two weeks ago, the shekel has been volatile but little changed.
Danny Alt, portfolio manager at Nesuah Trading and Investment, said the rise in CPI-linked bonds was also due to the fact that the government was issuing less of these bonds.

He said Makam prices rose nicely on Sunday because short-term expectations were that interest rates would fall due to forecasts for a low September CPI. He also said he expected the shekel would remain strong against the dollar.
September's CPI will be published on October 15.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
